headline: High-risk cloud-workspace agent paired with a non-interactive game-playing model creates dangerous default write and compliance exposure, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by B's lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read files, use MCP, and act autonomously in a shared integration environment, so malicious content in shared artifacts could influence it. LightZero has no filesystem, browser, or MCP surfaces, so there is no direct reverse channel from B into A beyond manual handoff. The pathway exists but is mostly manual and narrow.
conditions: IF a human copies LightZero output into Devin prompts or files
IF Devin is pointed at shared integration artifacts containing attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Restrict Devin to trusted folders only
Require human review before pasting B outputs into A
Disable MCP connectors for untrusted sources
Use a prompt-injection filter on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and can write to cloud workspace files and repo clones. LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not a meaningful exfiltration sink. Leakage risk is mainly from Devin exposing sensitive workspace data into shared integrations, not from B.
conditions: IF Devin is connected to repositories or chats containing secrets
IF Devin posts workspace content into Slack, Jira, or GitHub integrations
mitigations: Limit Devin to non-sensitive repos
Rotate any secrets present in shared workspaces
Disable Slack/Jira write scopes for sensitive projects
Review outbound messages before sync
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad shell, filesystem, git, and network write capabilities in a shared cloud workspace model. LightZero is non-runnable and has no write capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is absent. However, Devin's integrations and parallel sessions can still collide with shared repo or issue state if orchestrated poorly, making conflict plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF multiple Devin sessions target the same repo or issue tracker
IF shared integrations are writable by more than one session
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared repos
Assign one session per branch
Pause parallel Devin sessions on the same ticket
Use branch protection and required reviews
requires-engineering: add locking around shared integrations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can act autonomously and write to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, so if it consumes LightZero output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. LightZero is a game-playing model with no verification or downstream action controls, so the pair lacks an inherent check. The pathway is plausible whenever B's output is used as input to A.
conditions: IF LightZero output is pasted into Devin as facts or instructions
IF Devin is allowed to act on B-generated content without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on B output
Constrain Devin to draft-only mode for external actions
Add a verification step against source data
Mark B output as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware action gating

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a cloud workspace agent that handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and can write to Slack, Jira, and Notion, creating default compliance exposure for regulated or sensitive data. LightZero is open-source and non-runnable, so it adds no compensating compliance controls. Because Devin's default integrations can move data across services, the pair can breach residency or retention expectations without special setup.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Devin's connected workspace
IF Slack, Jira, or Notion contain data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Devin workspaces
Disable nonessential write integrations
Shorten retention on connected services
Review data-flow mappings before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and logging controls
